input.quote: EXCEPT FOR LIABILITY ARISING UNDER SECTION 8 OF THIS AGREEMENT, IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT OR THE USE OR PERFORMANCE OF THE SOFTWARE EXCEED THE TOTAL AMOUNT ACTUALLY PAID BY CORIO HEREUNDER FOR THE TRANSACTION WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES TO DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO THE FILING OF THE CAUSE OF ACTION TO WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES.
input.rationale: The cap in § 9 is mutual and the consequential-damages exclusion is mutual, which is good, but it fails the fallback on two material terms. First, the base is not 12 months' fees: it is only amounts "actually paid by Corio ... for the transaction which the liability relates to" in the prior 12 months, which slices the cap down to a single transaction's fees and can fall well below six months' fees (walk-away territory for a vendor cap). Second, the only carve-out is Section 8 (Commerce One's IP indemnity); there are no carve-outs for breach of confidentiality (§ 10 / the concurrent NDA), gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, whereas the fallback requires carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct. Redline moves the clause to the preferred position: greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and US$1,000,000, standard Excluded Claims outside the cap, and confirmation that Corio's fee obligations are not capped damages. Minor drafting notes not separately flagged: the duplicated consequential-damages sentence at p0092 appears to be a conversion artifact and the consequential-damages carve-out still cross-refers only to Section 8.

proposal.summary: Make the mutual cap a true 12-months'-fees floor of US$1,000,000 and add standard uncapped carve-outs
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We removed the "transaction which the liability relates to" narrowing so the mutual cap is the greater of twelve months' fees and US$1,000,000, which is our standard position. We also added the standard carve-outs so indemnification, confidentiality/security breaches, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sit outside the cap, and confirmed Corio's fee obligations are not capped damages.

ops.newText: EXCEPT FOR EXCLUDED CLAIMS, IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT OR THE USE OR PERFORMANCE OF THE SOFTWARE EXCEED THE GREATER OF (A) THE TOTAL AMOUNT PAID OR PAYABLE BY CORIO HEREUNDER DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CAUSE OF ACTION TO WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES AND (B) ONE MILLION U.S. DOLLARS (US$1,000,000). "EXCLUDED CLAIMS" MEANS A PARTY'S LIABILITY ARISING UNDER SECTION 8 OF THIS AGREEMENT, ITS BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY, DATA PROTECTION OR SECURITY OBLIGATIONS, ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE, WILFUL MISCONDUCT OR FRAUD, AND ITS INFRINGEMENT OF THE OTHER PARTY'S INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS. CORIO'S OBLIGATION TO PAY FEES DUE HEREUNDER SHALL NOT BE TREATED AS DAMAGES SUBJECT TO THIS SECTION 9.
